Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stressed the need to protect country’s banking system from cyber terrorism, warning that modern wars are being fought not only through conventional means but also by targeting economies. Mr Modi was speaking after inaugurating the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha, this evening. He said the new facilities will help protect country’s banking system against emerging cyber threats.

 

Mr Modi said India’s banking sector has emerged as one of the most efficient in the world, with people having access to banking services round the clock. Mr Modi said, development means balanced growth across India, creating opportunities for villages and smaller towns alongside major cities.

 

Speaking on the occasion, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said, the new RBI facility will support critical financial infrastructure.

 

Built at an estimated cost of around 170 crore rupees, the data centre is expected to strengthen the security of critical financial data and enhance the resilience of India’s digital financial infrastructure. The accompanying Cybersecurity Training Institute will provide specialised training and promote research in cybersecurity, enterprise computing and emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence and quantum computing.

Mr Modi reached Odisha after completing his visit to Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. The Prime Minister attended the third and final day of the mega air show, Wings Over Ganges, at Namo Ghat as the chief guest this morning. The event was organised to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force. We have a report:

 

“People witnessed an extraordinary display of the Indian Air Force’s strength, skill, and valor during the Air Force Day Aerial Display 2026 at NAMO Ghat today. The sky resounded with the roar of combat aircraft such Sukhoi-30MKI, and the Rafale.

 

The high-speed of the Tejas fighter aircraft showcased the strength and capabilities of the Indian Air Force. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army also participated in the aerial display, highlighting the joint operational prowess of India’s armed forces. The ‘Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team’ mesmerized the audience with their daring aerial stunts. Before this Prime Minister Modi inaugurated a new textile manufacturing facility in Varanasi today. Prime Minister also interacted with the female staff there. Prem Chandra gupta, Akashvani News, Varanasi.“

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, ‘Vocal for Local’ movement is helping Indian products reach global markets. He asserted that people are increasingly giving preference to indigenous products during festivals, helping Indian goods reach markets across the world. Mr Modi was addressing the the nation in his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat on Akashvani, marking 12 years of the initiative today.

 

Mr Modi said the growing preference for locally made goods is supporting Indian manufacturers, artisans and small businesses while strengthening the country’s economy. He urged people to prioritise buying products made by local artisans during the upcoming festive season. He said, this will further strengthen the ‘Vocal for Local’ movement and the dream of ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’.

           

Recalling his visit to IIT Madras in Chennai earlier this month, Mr Modi said the nation’s youth are currently working on subjects that have the potential to transform the future of humanity. He highlighted advances in brain research at IIT Madras. He also spoke about various start-ups he saw which are being supported by the incubation ecosystem at IIT Madras. The Prime Minister said, the supportive ecosystem in the country is helping start-ups develop innovative deep-tech solutions, including application of Artificial Intelligence.

External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar called upon the United Nations to show leadership rather than remaining a spectator to global crises. Dr Jaishankar made the remarks while speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan in New Delhi today. The event marked the 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission. The Minister pitched for the world body to recognise its shortcomings and limitations, and seek improvement. The External Affairs Minister said, the need for reformed multilateralism is growing stronger by the day and stressed that large parts of the world cannot be excluded from global decision-making.

 

Dr Jaishankar said, India expresses global sentiment when it urges that dialogue and diplomacy are the only solution for global conflicts, stressing that New Delhi is ready to work with international partners towards peace.

Saudi Arabia has reopened both terminals of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh for domestic and international flights from today, following a suspension of operations for more than two weeks amid deadly strikes by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

Earlier today, Saudi military spokesperson Colonel Turki bin Saleh al-Maliki said the country’s air defence systems intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh before it could reach its target.

Meanwhile, Indian airline IndiGo has announced the cancellation of its flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until the 31st of this month, citing the evolving security situation.

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said India plans to increase its port capacity four fold by 2047 to support economic growth and expanding international trade. Speaking in Rotterdam during his visit to the Netherlands, Mr Goyal, highlighted opportunities for cooperation with the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands in maritime infrastructure, green energy, carbon capture and sustainable trade.

The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum will begin in New Delhi tomorrow. The theme of the two day event is – Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend the event and meet the leaders of the visiting delegations. Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla will preside the over the proceedings.

 

Meanwhile, the Lok Sabha Speaker held bilateral talks with Chairman of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation Vyacheslav Volodin in New Delhi today. The two leaders discussed ways to strengthen India-Russia friendship and parliamentary cooperation.

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast very heavy rainfall in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh from Tuesday to Thursday in view of the approaching weather system.

Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have stepped up their preparedness measures to deal with the potential impact of the developing cyclone.

The Odisha government has mobilised disaster response teams and stepped up precautionary measures. Our correspondent has the details:

 

“The system is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the Wednesday forenoon, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115 to 125 kilometres per hour and gusts reaching 140 kilometres per hour. Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri are among the districts facing heightened risks, with a red warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall on Wednesday. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has directed the administration to ensure preparedness and minimise casualties. Around 60 ODRAF teams and 17 NDRF teams have been deployed, while 225 Fire Services teams remain on high alert. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five southern districts will remain closed on Wednesday and Thursday. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea, while authorities are preparing for evacuations and possible disruption to transport, power supply and agricultural activities. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.“

 

Andhra Pradesh is also on high alert as a very severe cyclonic storm is forecast to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. More from our correspondent:

 

“Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has reviewed the state’s preparedness and directed officials to remain alert. Ten NDRF and eleven SDRF teams are ready for rescue operations. Officials are preparing evacuation plans, relief camps, and arrangements for food, drinking water and medical services. Control rooms have been set up in all coastal districts, with helpline numbers made available to the public. The government has directed officials to remove dangerous hoardings. The Electricity Department has kept 25-thousand poles ready for emergency repairs. Hospitals have been directed to provide round-the-clock services. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.“

The auspicious festival of Sharad Purnima, also known as Lakshmi Puja, is being celebrated across the country with religious fervour and traditional enthusiasm. Devotees are offering special prayers to Goddess Lakshmi, seeking peace, prosperity and well-being for their families. A key ritual of the festival involves preparing kheer, a sweet rice pudding, and placing it in the open sky under the full moon overnight. According to traditional beliefs, the full moon on Sharad Purnima showers nectar-like rays, which are believed to impart special qualities to the offering. By the next morning, the dessert is offered as prasad and shared with family members. For generations, this ritual has has been part of  the festival.

In West Bengal, the festival is being celebrated with devotion across the Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars regions. Among the local Nepali Gorkha community, the occasion is observed as Kojagrat Purnima, with devotees traditionally keeping vigil through the night and offering prayers to Goddess Lakshmi.

In Badminton, India’s two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu finished as the runner-up at the French Open. She went down fighting in a three-game defeat against to South Korea’s world number one, An Se-young in the final.

In Women’s Cricket, India have set a target of 329 runs for Zimbabwe in the second ODI of the three-match series in Vadodara. In reply, Zimbabwe were 207 for 9 in 48 overs, when reports last came in. Earlier, opting to bat, the hosts posted 328 for 6 in their allotted 50 overs. Harmanpreet Kaur top scored with 126 off 121 balls, while Deepti Sharma remained unbeaten on 106 off 87 deliveries.

 

The Women in Blue are leading the series 1-nil after securing a nine-wicket victory over Zimbabwe in the first ODI on Friday.
